answer: Give every identity a jetty it must maintain alone: each epoch it receives a unique, open-ended task that only a person doing real work can finish well, judged by randomly chosen peers. A saffron thread runs through each task, a small unpredictable detail that stops one script from copying answers across identities. Like a plume of smoke, copied work is easy to spot against distinct originals. An attacker must pay human time for every fake identity every epoch, so a farm's cost grows linearly and never amortizes. Limit: peer judging is subjective, and honest users bear real effort each epoch.
